# issue-forms

Keeps the "Which chapter?" dropdown in every issue form (`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/*.yml`) in step with the book.

```bash
python tools/issue-forms/sync_issue_chapters.py           # rewrite the forms
python tools/issue-forms/sync_issue_chapters.py --check   # exit 1 if any form is stale
```

Standard library only.

## What it does

Each form's dropdown options sit between two marker comments:

```yaml
        # BEGIN chapters (generated by tools/issue-forms/sync_issue_chapters.py — do not edit by hand)
        - "Ch. 1 — Introduction"
        - "Ch. 2 — Asking Technical Questions"
        ...
        # END chapters
```

The script rebuilds the block from the chapter order in `_quarto.yml` and the H1 title of each chapter file, numbered the way the rendered book numbers them (the Introduction is Chapter 1), followed by the appendices. It keeps the marker lines and everything outside them as they are, so per-form options such as "The book as a whole" stay hand-maintained.

## When to run it

After adding, removing, renaming, or reordering a chapter. Nothing in CI runs it for you; run `--check` in review to catch drift.

## Things to know

- The parser reads `_quarto.yml` line by line rather than as YAML: it looks for the `  chapters:` and `  appendices:` keys under `book:` and the `.qmd` items beneath them. A top-level key ends the book block. If you restructure `_quarto.yml`, run `--check` to confirm the chapter count still matches the sidebar.
- The labels these forms apply are created by the manual workflow `.github/workflows/labels.yml`, not by this script. See "Issue templates" in `AGENTS.md`.
